leverage.exposure: No leveraged position, and none is being opened — the only recommended action is a sale, which increases the balance. The real exposure is the opposite: after the sale the squad sits below the eleven-man floor and must be refilled before the next lock. There is ample time, but it is now a standing obligation rather than a preference, and it is the single thing a future run must not let slide. A smaller, unhedgeable exposure remains in goal, where Georg carries a single keeper who has already missed one matchday to rotation this season; with no bench there is nothing to do about it.

binding_gap: The weakest fielded body by a wide margin is Sirch, and in the only legal formation this squad can fill there is no bench to hide him on. Every previous run refused to sell him because the squad sat at exactly eleven, and this run originally deferred the sale for the same underlying worry. Both were wrong for the same reason: the floor is a matchday-start test, not a continuous one, and the next lock is three weeks away. So the sale goes first and the replacement is found at leisure. The obligation this creates must be carried by every subsequent run and said out loud each time: Georg must be back to eleven players before the next lock or he takes the full penalty. The likely refill is not on the board yet.

verdict.headline: Sell Sirch now, before tonight's market-value tick.
verdict.headline_short: Sell Sirch now, before tonight's market-value tick.
verdict.detail: Sell Sirch now, before tonight's market-value tick. Georg corrected the rule this run: the eleven-player floor is checked at matchday start, not continuously. Matchday four started Thursday with eleven placed, so that test is passed and cannot be failed retroactively — selling into a live matchday carries no penalty risk and the keeper's banked score is safe. The earlier gate on this run's briefing, which held the sale until Elversberg had played on Sunday, is withdrawn. Waiting would have crossed two daily value ticks and cost real money for no benefit. No buy: after the sale the envelope is still too small for anything on the board that actually plays, so hold the cash and shop a board that turns over several times a day.

sell.reason: Sirch, now, by instant sale to Kickbase. He is fit but out of Elversberg's eleven on a dated club-by-club source, his last two appearances were late cameos and he was an unused substitute in the matchday before this one. In the only legal shape this squad can field, every outfield player is fielded, so he cannot be benched — he is a guaranteed near-zero in the eleven every week. The instant sale pays exactly market value, so the price is known. The timing matters: values tick once daily in the evening and he is falling steadily, so selling before tonight's tick is worth meaningfully more than selling after Elversberg play on Sunday. The one genuine cost of selling mid-matchday is forfeiting whatever he would still have scored, and for him that is a small cameo chance at best — the preserved value is the better side of that trade. Note the general form of that test though: it is decided per player. Selling a confirmed starter whose club has not yet played would forfeit real points and should wait for his fixture. Everyone else stays. In particular ter Horst is not a sale despite his sliding value — he starts nearly every minute for his club, and selling a real starter to fund an upgrade elsewhere costs more points than it buys.

MERIT, UNCHANGED: ap 18, the weakest fielded body by 64 points, and in 5-3-2 with exactly eleven players he cannot be benched. He is fit - he has lost his place, not been injured out of it.

Nineteen days, a board that turns over several times daily, and the best-identified target is Ullrich (WATCH Wmf9t12) at 4.396.254 - still outside the envelope, so the refill most likely comes from a listing not yet on the board.

buy.reason: Nothing, and the reason is the envelope rather than the board. Even after the Sirch money lands, the cash available is small, and every listing inside it fails on merit: a Bremen defender who has never played a competitive minute and whose club is still talking about getting him fit in friendlies, a flagged Gladbach defender with no record at all, and three bodies with negative or near-zero averages.
